status: Shape-led abstract material and sparse ornament concepts; not implemented Unity assets

maps.name: Tideway Metropolis
maps.fit: Use the central ring-capped stack as a contrasting material anchor, the long radial bridges for directional grain, and the low folded structures for smaller-scale shell, fiber or resin details.
themes: Tall thin frame stacks: dark wet slate posts and pale opaque chalk tops, vivid turquoise mineral strata only on slab sides; center ring-capped stack: pearly cream posts with coral-orange side veins, a contrasting anchor. Branching slabs: green-blue nacre ripple patterns. Low courtyard and folded slabs: bleached timber grain with sand-polished edges and occasional small shell clusters on EXTERIOR corners. Bridges: neutral pale stone tops, tide-line bands on sides. A few short salt-crystal growths under OUTSIDE deck edges; no detail curtains. Warm sea mist, turquoise ocean, pale sandy island with flat tide-pattern textures.

Tall narrow stacks: charcoal posts and brushed silver opaque deck tops, irregular violet oil-slick slab SIDES and a few chunky chrome joint caps. Central ring stack: warm ivory speckled ceramic posts with magenta luminous hairline cracks; branching slabs: cyan anodized-metal sides with dark quiet tops. Low pavilions: peach/gray ceramic with large stipple patterns and sparse pink resin beads underneath outside corners. Do not put emission on every edge. Deep purple midnight sky with bright ambient fill, blue-black ocean, charcoal patterned island.

Central branching structures: rich grooved bark posts, amber-resin side plates with trapped bubble patterns; tall rear stacks: cool blue-gray basalt posts, ivory opaque top faces, turquoise quartz veins in sides. Ring-capped center stack: pale smooth wood and warm yellow translucent-looking resin SIDES, opaque tops. Low courts: warm clay ceramic with broad lichen patches and little dried seed-pod decorations under outside edges. Sparse curved root collars attached to a few exterior post bases, no vines over grip faces. Warm hazy dawn, moss/ochre island texture, muted green sea.

maps.name: Double-Loop Exchange
maps.fit: Use the two route loops for two interacting material families. Let the shared exchange stacks combine those families by whole slabs, while low pavilions inherit the nearest loop.
themes: One entire loop has dark magnetic iron posts with broad brushed-grain slab sides and cool silver tops; the other has cream porous ceramic posts and thick orange wax-like marbled slab sides with matte cream tops. At shared taller exchange stacks, interleave BOTH families in distinct full slabs instead of random color pieces. Low pavilions follow closest loop but display sparse bead-like iron nodules or small wax-drip shapes on outside undersides. Bridge junctions get a few chunky coupling rings wrapped on outside ends, no rails. Night blue sky, dark neutral island, warm reflective cobalt sea. Meaning is sculptural material contrast, not transport architecture.

Outer loop slab faces are chalk white with broad lavender salt bands, cream speckled columns and blue-gray tops; inner loop has dark driftwood posts, glossy petrol-green side stripes and pale worn timber tops. Shared skyline towers have contrasting black basalt posts and alternating pale salt / green kelp-pattern slab edges. Low courts near white loop have tiny crystal corner clusters, low courts near wood loop have a few short kelp ribbons attached UNDER outside edges. Coupled textures show contact at junctions. Soft white sky, pale salt island, muted rose-blue ocean. No new trees or slippery water surfaces.

Outer slabs: smoky violet resin SIDE faces with embedded broken light filaments, opaque matte lilac tops, cream posts. Inner slabs: turquoise rubberized sides with big faded coral stipples, dark blue posts, pale gray tops. Tall shared stacks: graphite posts and opaque steel tops, alternate resin/rubber slabs coherent by floor. A few chrome puck details at selected bridge joints and little cable-loop shapes on EXTERIOR post backs. Lower pavilions inherit one family each, not all same paint. Starry peach-blue dusk, dark speckled island, purple ocean. Filaments are surface art, no energy hazard.

maps.name: Caldera Switchback City
maps.fit: Use the existing rise from bowl to high crowns for a coarse-to-refined material progression. Give the wide inclined saddle panels a different surface pattern from the narrow upright stacks.
themes: Bowl-low structures: dark porous volcanic posts and layered rust/orange slab edges, quiet pale ash tops. East ascent: teal mineral streaks through gray stone; west ascent: warm amber banding through buff stone. High saddle tower's slanted panels: broad smoky quartz facets painted as opaque surface detail, few small crystal tips attached to their OUTSIDE corners. Other high stacks: chalk-white posts and blue-gray top slabs with pale opal sides. Low basin pavilions get dark iron crust and tiny green crystal clusters under outer edges. Ground follows existing bowl with dark-to-light mineral TEXTURE bands, no new pool or crater. Copper dawn, blue sea.

Low bowl slabs are clay-red with glossy imperfect glaze pools on SIDE faces, cream matte tops, dark umber posts. East switchbacks: cobalt crackle glaze and pale stone posts; west: jade crackle glaze with ochre posts. High saddle's wide inclined slabs have pearly flowing glaze streaks, contrasting the narrow upper stack's charcoal/silver surfaces. A few bead-like glaze drips hang only beneath exterior corners, very sparse. Low folded courts have rough bisque posts and speckled ivory tops. Clear soft sky, ochre ceramic-looking ground texture, deep cobalt ocean. No literal kiln building or new geometry enclosing frames.

Lower structures: rough black-blue fossil stone posts with broad cream spiral imprints; side slabs dark plum with pale fossil bands, opaque gray tops. Mid ramps: green oxidized mineral sides and cream supports. High saddle broad slopes: smooth bone-ivory plates with blue crystalline grain; tall opposite stack: dark charcoal columns with restrained cyan seams. Sparse small fossil-shell collars on exterior bases and one or two ice-like shard clusters under high OUTSIDE corners. Low courts vary between rough fossil stone and smoother bone plates by height. Indigo aurora sky with daylight-like fill, gray-purple ground, ink-teal sea. No giant bones replacing supports.

maps.name: Broken Crown Capital
maps.fit: Use the separated crown fragments as different cross-sections of one material world, with quieter connecting slabs and small accent details on exterior fragment edges.
themes: Each separated outer crown fragment exposes a different geode cross-section: west dark rough basalt posts and amethyst slab sides; northeast silver-gray posts with turquoise crystalline sides; eastern paired frame ivory stone with honey-amber banded sides. The off-center tallest ring-capped beacon is contrasting pearl-white and very dark indigo with thin gold mineral seams. Low interior courts are rough gray/cream stone with small amethyst or aqua patches based on nearby fragment. Tiny crystal clusters at a handful of EXTERIOR broken-looking corners only, no spikes on walking tops. Bridges neutral opaque stone, seams change at joints. Lavender dawn, mineral island, blue sea.

West broad fragmented slabs: warm red lacquer sides with black fibrous wood posts. Northeast thin tower: cool oxidized copper posts and pale stone decks; eastern gateway-like frames: mustard enamel side plates and navy posts. Central tall landmark: bone ceramic posts and deep burgundy side marbling. Low pavilions mix chipped enamel/timber/stone distinctly by local cluster, with very few chunky metallic rivet caps and small leaf-shaped hammered metal tabs under outside corners. Big surface wear patches, not high-frequency noise. Amber dusk, neutral dark island, slate ocean. Remains abstract sculptural assembly, not palace walls.

West crown slabs: smoky raspberry glass-like SIDES but opaque cream tops, dark cocoa posts. Northeast tower: cool gray basalt frame and mint-swirled slab sides. Eastern paired slabs: apricot resin and ivory speckled posts. Tall off-center anchor: dark blue frame with opaline ivory side panels. Low interior courts: matte biscuit ceramic and sparse glossy candy-pebble trim under edges; no giant candy props. Only a few translucent-looking sugar-crystal clusters under exterior slab corners. Pearl-pink cloud sky, pale lavender sand, blue-green sea; preserve block seams and no transparent walking surfaces.

maps.name: Harbor Loom
maps.fit: Use the long horizontal weave to contrast lengthwise fiber/strata textures with vertical weathering on tall posts. Give the stepped frames a third surface family.
themes: Low wide foundry-like slabs: coarse pale timber grain with terracotta woven-fiber SIDE bands, dark brown posts. Tall skinny stacks: cool blue-gray mineral posts and clean cream top faces, turquoise tide-stain sides. Stepped waterworks frame: pale coral-stone posts with pink nacre side strips. Central low interchange: gray slate tops with radial fossil imprints only on side faces. A few shell clusters at post bases and short rope-like fiber loops under selected EXTERIOR joints; no dock props or literal shipping office signs. Different physical shapes carry different fiber/stone/shell treatments. Golden noon, pale island, aquamarine sea.

Horizontal wide slabs have dark oxidized copper sides with irregular green patina islands, quiet slate tops and iron posts. Narrow tall stack: pale ceramic posts and dark pearlescent blue sides; stepped frames: rich brown wood and cream/faded gold. Low courts alternate rough fossil stone and copper-rimmed pale tops by proximity, not all copper. Tiny barnacle clusters and a few black pearl-like beads attached to selected column BACKS and undersides, not free particles. Dim warm storm-break sky with strong fill, dark pebble island, deep green ocean. No containers, ship props, signs or enclosed buildings.

Wide stacked slabs: orange molded-plastic sides with broad irregular cream swirls, navy posts and matte gray tops. Taller thin stack: silver posts and violet resin sides with embedded bubble textures; stepped towers: mint ceramic and dark graphite. Low folded slabs: peach rubberized sides, speckled ivory tops, chunky blue joint caps. Sparse small chrome coupling rings and tiny amber crystal nubs on outside ends, no added functional machinery. Blue dusk sky, dark slate island with subtle large-scale stripe texture, purple sea. Visually diverse found objects assembled into abstract shapes, not a port.

maps.name: Lantern Ravine
maps.fit: Emphasize diagonal grain and underside detail on the leaning compression frames. Contrast their surfaces with the upright ridge stacks and rougher low ravine courts.
themes: Leaning compression frames: dark fibrous bark columns with silky coral-pink gill textures on deck UNDERSIDES, pale opaque leaf-green tops. West stepped blocks: warm reddish porous stone and golden lichen side patches. East upright skyline: cool wet slate posts and pearly blue mineral side bands. High ring-capped stack: pale bone posts and warm amber side seams. Low ravine pavilions: mossed gray stone and irregular ivory top patches; a few tiny luminous seed-pod clusters under external lips and short hanging leaves on outward sides. No heavy vines or new trees. Warm mist at distant horizon only, violet twilight, dark green island, teal sea.

Leaning frames: deep navy posts, opaque pearl tops, broad lavender ice-striation sides that emphasize diagonal compression. Upright ridge tower: warm ochre/copper posts and gray deck tops, strong contrast. West stepped structures: blue-gray stone with chalk-white weathering; high ring stack ivory and turquoise vein patterns. Low courts: rough charcoal and pale mineral-tile tops, a few tiny ice-crystal clusters attached under exterior edges only. Frost is visual, not extra collision or slippery movement. Aurora green and indigo sky with generous fill, pale textured island shoulders, deep navy sea. No new snow banks or iceberg props.

Leaning frames have dark charcoal-bark posts with a few small emerald/blue iridescent beetle-shell plates ATTACHED to outward faces, floors remain simple opaque warm gray with turquoise vein SIDES. West step stacks use honey wood and matte cream; east tall stack uses deep violet stone and silver side streaks; high ring beacon warm amber resin sides and bone posts. Low pavilions are rough pinkish mineral stone with tiny shell scales only near exterior joints, clear pillar grip faces. No actual insects, giant legs or altered silhouettes. Warm amber sky against cool dark island and blue ocean; subdued specular away from shell details.

maps.name: Canopy Borough
maps.fit: Exploit the three branching crowns: their wide tops, visible undersides and posts can carry different textures. Keep the narrow skyline and low folded courts materially distinct.
themes: Branching crowns use leaf-veined tops and cream-to-coral gilled undersides on bark posts; west is dry red bark/gold, center jade, east pale lichen/blue-green. Narrow skyline contrasts dark wet stone and sparse small iridescent shell plates. Low courts use porous mossed stone, a few small mushrooms and exterior hanging leaves. Original abstract frames and routes remain open. Warm humid sky, dark leaf-litter ground texture, teal sea.

Branching crowns show pearlescent shell SIDE faces, pale opaque sea-glass tops and pink gill-like undersides on porous coral-stone posts. Dark basalt skyline contrasts cyan mineral veins and a few barnacle clusters. Low courtyards use bleached timber, sandstone, tide rings and sparse exterior shell accents. Original slab silhouettes remain the reference. Pale mineral island, clear sea-mist sky, aqua ocean.

Central slabs have smoky violet resin sides with embedded filaments and matte lilac tops; west molded orange plastic; east cracked mint ceramic. Tall skyline graphite and thin lime seams. Low pavilions peach/turquoise rubberized sides with sparse chrome corner nodes. Keep all paths opaque and clear, original geometry open. Dark speckled rubber-like island, purple sea, peach dusk.

maps.name: Bookfall Boulevard
maps.fit: Put large-scale texture compositions on the existing broad Book Wing panels; use alternating finishes on the Zipper's staggered slabs. Smaller low courts provide quieter tactile detail.
themes: Broad Book Wing side walls: large overlapping pressed-leaf textures and fibrous parchment bands, not literal printed books. Their open slabs have warm cream tops and dark green undersides; posts pale speckled stone. Zipper tower: contrasting black slate posts with alternating opaline white and copper side faces, emphasizing staggered teeth; civic tall tower: warm red-brown wood and thin amber veins. Low courts vary cream fossil-stone and dark bark with small curled leaf or seed-pod clusters under OUTSIDE edges only. Broad near-vertical existing panels carry low-frequency natural patterns. Soft golden sky, parchment mineral island, dark ink-blue sea.

Broad Book Wing panels display big cobalt/cream cracked-glaze islands with terracotta borders; slabs opaque celadon tops with creamy undersides, dark blue stone posts. Zipper tower: metallic gray posts and pearly pink side strips on alternating projecting slabs; civic tower: rough warm ochre posts and ivory side plates. Low courts use rough bisque and muted lilac glaze with a few small glazed ceramic fragments attached to exterior corners like scales. No dish props, signs or buildings. Patterns exploit existing broad panels and staggered deck edges. Pale ground, clear sky, deep cobalt sea.

Broad wing panels: dark woven-carbon pattern with large irregular violet/blue oil-slick patches, floors matte pale gray and sides smoky amber resin. Zipper stack: bone ceramic posts and alternating turquoise/charcoal side bands, huge material contrast. Civic tower: brushed copper posts and warm ivory plates. Low pavilions: rubberized peach and gray with sparse small chrome domes on exterior backs, no actual vinyl records or speaker props. A few embedded bubble-like shapes under resin exterior corners; opaque walkable tops. Plum dusk sky, charcoal island, violet ocean.

maps.name: Three Hearts City
maps.fit: Differentiate the major structural clusters, keep the central catch tower's ledges visually clear, and let the low pieces connect material families without repeating one finish everywhere.
themes: Gateway-shaped northwest structure: dark volcanic posts and jade mineral banded deck sides. Spiral north: ivory speckled posts and warm copper/pink shell-striation sides following stacked rotation. Hotel-like paired northeast frames: smoky violet stone posts and opal blue sides. CENTRAL catch tower: contrasting cream ceramic posts and quiet gray tops with sparse gold fine cracks, keep catch ledges clear and visibly broad. Waterfront low wide slabs: dark bark with honey tops. Low pavilions inherit nearest mineral family; central ones use cream, bridges neutral gray. Small seed-like crystal clusters under a few OUTSIDE slabs, no doors, windows, city signs. Warm misty sky, dark mineral island, teal sea.
Molded toy, aged metal, cracked ceramic

Northwest gateway: orange molded-plastic side faces with broad marbling, dark blue posts; northern spiral: brushed copper posts, ivory decks and muted green patina on sides; northeast paired frames: pale mint cracked ceramic and graphite supports. Central catch tower: warm lilac resin SIDE faces, cream posts, opaque pearl tops; no pretend elevator or skyscraper facade. Lower wide slabs and pavilions mix rubberized coral/gray near plastic, buff ceramic near spiral, pale blue near mint. Sparse external chrome bolt domes and one tiny coil on selected post backs only. Soft lavender sky, charcoal speckled island, blue-purple sea. Keep structure differences legible even without text.
Tide pool after the world dried

Northwest gateway has rough reddish coral-stone posts and opaque pale blue tops, white calcified slab sides. Spiral is black wet basalt and turquoise/purple nacre-stripe sides. Northeast paired frames are bleached timber and warm pink salt bands. Central catch tower stands out with pearl-white mineral frame and deep green underside textures, no transparency. Low pavilions have sand-polished stone, tide-ring surface marks and little shell or barnacle clusters attached low on OUTSIDE pillars. Keep original geometry and no added pools or trees. Pale salt island with flat blue tide-texture patches, bright hazy sky, clear aqua ocean.

maps.name: The Rising Spine
maps.fit: Use the actual seaside-to-summit elevation sequence for changing grain, porosity and sheen. Contrast the stepped middle structure, pale summit and darker return-side skyline.
themes: Lowest wide slabs: rough dark bark posts, moss and ochre grain SIDE faces, gray quiet tops. Middle stepped relay: copper-brown porous posts and amber resin sides with bubble textures, opaque cream tops. Highest inland ring-capped stack: pale ivory mineral posts and blue opal side veins, a clear material progression by elevation. Secondary skyline on return side: dark slate and silver, contrasting the ivory summit. Low courts follow altitude with bark, rough stone, then pale ceramic; a few small seed pods and crystal clusters outside edges, not on routes. Existing terrain unchanged with brown-to-chalk TEXTURE gradient; pale blue sky, silver sea. No literal summit temple or cloud platforms.

Low market-shaped slabs: chipped orange enamel sides and dark navy posts; first terraces: rough gray stone with ochre stripes. Middle relay: rich teal oxidized-copper columns and cream matte slabs; upper summit: silver posts with violet resin side panels and opaque pale gray tops. Return skyline: brick-red lacquer and charcoal; shoulder low courts cream/teal, lower courts rust/gray. Sparse small metal tabs and chrome joint caps attached at EXTERIOR corners, avoid functional machinery props. Broad wear patterns exploit faces, not detailed building facades. Storm-break sky, ochre textured island, green-blue sea, strong ambient light.

Low wide structures: charcoal fossil-stone columns, cream spiral imprints on SIDE panels and warm gray deck tops. Middle stepped structure: dark violet stone and jade nacre bands. Summit tall stack: porous bone-ivory posts and restrained cyan crystalline side seams, no extra ribs or giant bones. Return skyline: blue-black mineral with copper highlights. Low pavilions have pale rough stone, velvety purple moss patterns and very few small luminous seed-pod clusters UNDER exterior edges. Existing height sequence drives changing textures; no houses, offices or temple signs. Indigo sky and aurora backdrop with bright horizon fill, dark purple island with pale paths, teal-black ocean.
